title: Puzzle book method: from a chosen theme to a large-print KDP paperback and printable twin
ends_with: The owner holds the print interior PDF, the full cover PDF, the printable twin files (Letter, A4, start-here, terms, free sample), the verification report, a paste-ready listing kit in the order KDP asks for it and the direct upload link, all in the brand folder linked on the job in HQ.

outside_hq.what: Make sure the one KDP account is ready: tax interview and bank details done.
outside_hq.why: KDP will not pay royalties without them, and the account rule is one account forever, never a second one.
outside_hq.how_owner_does_it: Sign in at kdp.amazon.com, open Your Account at the top, finish any section marked incomplete. Skip this if it is already done.

outside_hq.what: Make sure a Payhip account exists for the brand, and an Etsy shop if the twin goes on Etsy too.
outside_hq.why: The printable twin and the free sample are sold and delivered there; HQ cannot create accounts for him.
outside_hq.how_owner_does_it: Open payhip.com and etsy.com/sell, sign up with the brand email, connect payouts. Skip any that already exist.

outside_hq.what: Receive the printed proof copy in the mail and check it in hand, if he ordered one.
outside_hq.why: Only paper shows whether the letters really read as large print at arm's length, whether grids sink into the spine and whether answer marks are dark enough.
outside_hq.how_owner_does_it: When the box arrives, follow the proof checklist in stage 8 and tap pass or fail for each line in HQ.

outside_hq.what: Click Publish on KDP, Payhip and Etsy.
outside_hq.why: Agents never publish or upload on his behalf without his explicit yes; the final button on each site is his.
outside_hq.how_owner_does_it: Paste each field from the upload kit in the order shown, then press the publish button named in the kit.

outside_hq.what: Only if the agents are blocked on Amazon: phone screenshots of the 1 to 3 star reviews on the top five competing puzzle books.
outside_hq.why: Amazon restricts AI agents, and the review read must never run from the KDP publishing login.
outside_hq.how_owner_does_it: Open each of the five books in the Amazon app, filter reviews to 1, 2 and 3 stars, screenshot them and drop the images in the brand folder.

stages.title: Check the shelf and mine the reviews
stages.what: Study the top 20 competing puzzle books for the main search phrase (for example dog word search large print) and turn their buyers' complaints into a short list of things this book will fix.
stages.why: Puzzle buyers review the object: print that is not really large, wrong answer keys, missing words. Their repeated complaints are the cheapest proof of what to fix. For the Dog Lover's book this step is still open in HQ.
inputs: existing competitor check in HQ (for the Dog Lover's book: two dog word search books ranked about #11k with 92 reviews and about #104k with 10 reviews, October 16, 2026)

decided.value: Top 20 books for the main search phrase; read reviews on the top five most closely
decided.reason: His KDP Charter sets 20 for books.

decided.value: All 1, 2 and 3 star reviews plus the but-sentence in 4 star reviews, keeping 1 star reviews
decided.reason: His standard keeps 1 star reviews because they hold the print-size, key and layout failures; the NotebookLM advice to skip them was rejected at merge.

decided.value: Amazon reads go to Muse through the HQ agent mailbox, ChatGPT as backup, never the KDP login. If blocked: freely readable copies (Barnes and Noble, Walmart, eBay, Goodreads and mirror stores that show Amazon reviews), then phone screenshots from the owner as the last resort
decided.reason: Amazon restricts AI agents; the free copies already show the shelf's main complaints (print too small, word list on another page, too few words).

decided.what: Whether a low score stops the book
decided.value: No. The score ranks and sharpens the brief; it never blocks a title he picked.
decided.reason: Override of November 13, 2026.

work: Load the brand kit and the brand rules from HQ (for Big Paws Club: brand rules v1.1).
Run the free validation: search suggestions, top 20 results, sales rank read as relative, page counts, trim, puzzle counts and list prices.
Request the Amazon review and rank reads from Muse through the HQ agent mailbox, with ChatGPT as backup.

Cluster the complaints into the shelf's known groups (print size, layout, key, words, theme, difficulty, paper and binding), count how many books and reviewers repeat each, and quote each at ten words or fewer with its link.
Note what five-star reviews praise (big bold letters, themes that fit, word list beside the grid, mixed difficulty, thick pages); these are must-keeps.
File each complaint in the Answer Bank (audience_pains) and update the title's notes in HQ.

output.name: Complaint list with links and counts
output.lands_in: the title's notes in HQ and the Answer Bank

output.name: Top 20 shelf table (rank, ratings, price, pages, trim, puzzle count, stated point size)
output.lands_in: the brand folder, linked on the job in HQ

stages.check: At least five complaint groups are filed, each with a quote of ten words or fewer and a working link.
checks: The shelf table holds price and page count for at least ten books.
The five-star praise list has at least three items.
stages.if_fail: Widen to the second search phrase (for example large print word search for seniors) and repeat. This stage never blocks later stages for a book already built; its findings feed the listing and the stage 6 check.

stages.title: Approve the one-screen brief
stages.what: Claude fills the brief: buyer, puzzle type, the one theme, the list of sub-themes, puzzle count, difficulty mix, specs, the complaints it fixes and the price. The owner picks the price and the author name, then approves.
stages.why: Puzzle count, grid size and key layout set the page count, and the page count sets the printing cost, the royalty and the spine. Settling them here prevents the most expensive late change.

choices.question: What list price on Amazon.com?
choices.help: KDP pays 60 percent minus printing at $9.99 and up, 50 percent below. For the Dog Lover's book (156 pages after rounding) printing is about $3.65, so you earn about $4.14 at $12.99, $2.34 at $9.99 and $5.34 at $14.99. Comparable large-print word search books sell at $12.99 to $17.95.

options.pick_when: You want the low end of the shelf's price band with almost twice the royalty of $9.99.

options.label: $9.99 (the October 16 price)
options.pick_when: You want the cheapest impulse gift on the page and accept about $2.34 a copy.
The book has more than 100 puzzles or reviews already show it beats the shelf.

choices.question: Whose name goes on the cover as author?
choices.help: KDP allows a pen name or brand name as long as it does not mislead buyers. The same name must match on the cover, the title page and the KDP Author field.

options.label: The brand name (for example Big Paws Club)
options.pick_when: It is a brand puzzle book; sibling books will share the name.

options.label: Allmighty Supreme
options.pick_when: The book sits on your personal brand.

choices.question: Is the brief right?
choices.help: Read the one screen, including the sub-theme list. Approving starts the word lists; nothing is generated before this.

options.label: Approve
options.pick_when: The buyer, the theme and the sub-themes sound right.

options.label: Change something (say it by voice)
options.pick_when: A sub-theme, the count or the difficulty mix is off.

decided.value: Not ticked
decided.reason: KDP lists puzzle books as not generally low-content and says a wrong box gets the book rejected. Not ticking keeps the free ISBN, Look Inside, series and Expanded Distribution.

decided.value: Paperback plus printable twin; no Kindle edition
decided.reason: KDP's content quality guide lists puzzle books under content unsuited for reading on Kindle and says they are better suited to a physical form.

decided.value: 8.5 x 11 in, black ink, white paper, no bleed
decided.reason: 8.5 x 11 holds one large-print grid per page and runs 24 to 590 pages on white paper. White matches his seniors test (black on white); APH also allows ivory and never gray.

decided.value: One theme per volume (for example dogs), with one named sub-theme per puzzle (breeds, dog park, puppy days, famous dogs) and every word fitting its sub-theme
decided.reason: Mixed-bag books earn the no-themes review; his standard sets one theme per volume.

decided.value: 50 to 100 puzzles; a third each easy, medium and hard, labeled on every page, getting harder through the book
decided.reason: His standard sets 50 to 80; 100 is kept for the Dog Lover's book because it is already built and competitors sell 100 to 200. Too-easy and too-few-words are repeated complaints.

decided.value: Front matter about 6 pages, one puzzle per page, a divider, answer keys 2 per page; always an even total
decided.reason: KDP rounds the page count up to an even number, so an odd file changes the spine. 100 puzzles come to about 156 pages.

decided.value: Yes, a large-print book from the start, with the actual letter size stated in the subtitle
decided.reason: Older buyers are the main lane; APH sets 18 pt as the floor for anything called large print.

decided.value: Free KDP ISBN
decided.reason: Available because the book is not low-content; the imprint shows as Independently published.

decided.value: Fill the Series field from book one when the brief plans siblings (for example Big Paws Club Large-Print Puzzles, book 1)
decided.reason: Puzzle books can join a series; only low-content and public domain books cannot.

decided.value: At most two new paperbacks a week across all brands
decided.reason: KDP limit: up to 2 new titles per format each week, resetting Sunday 00:00 UTC.

decided.value: Plan for 3 to 4 weeks of KDP review
decided.reason: KDP says reviews for activity books, which include puzzle books, might take 3 to 4 weeks. A book uploaded in late November may miss Christmas.

work: Fill the brief template (kdp-book kit-contract.md section 1) with the puzzle fields: type, theme, sub-theme list, count, difficulty mix, grid sizes, words per puzzle, key layout.
Work out the page count and show the royalty at each price option with the math.
Book the KDP week slot in HQ.
Register the title on HQ's Products page at status scored, then brief once approved (kdp-book hq-recipes.md).

output.name: Approved brief with sub-theme list and page math
output.format: one screen in the job, plus brief.md
output.lands_in: the brand folder, linked on the job in HQ

stages.check: The owner tapped Approve, and the brief names the buyer, the theme, every sub-theme, the puzzle count, the page count and the price.
checks: The page count is even and the royalty at the chosen price is shown.
The low-content box is recorded as not ticked.
stages.if_fail: Claude rewrites the brief from his voice note and shows it again. If he skips the brief, Claude uses the recommended options and the card says the brief was not read.

skip.rule: The recommended option is used for every choice and the brief is approved as written.

stages.title: Build and check the themed word lists
stages.what: Claude writes one word list per puzzle from its sub-theme, then checks every word for spelling, fit, length, overlap and words that must not appear.
stages.why: Misspelled words, random words that do not fit the theme and an unalphabetized list are repeated one-star complaints, and a word hidden inside another word makes a grid unsolvable.

decided.value: Easy 12 to 15, medium 15 to 20, hard 18 to 24
decided.reason: His spec is 12 to 24 words per grid; a buyer complained about only 9 words a page.

decided.value: 4 to 12 letters, no spaces or punctuation inside the grid (GOLDEN RETRIEVER becomes GOLDENRETRIEVER in the grid and stays two words in the list)
decided.reason: Long words must fit the grid; short words appear by accident too often to count as found once.

decided.value: Spelled correctly (dictionary plus a second model read), fits its sub-theme, no trademark or brand name, no word inside another word in the same list, list alphabetized
decided.reason: His generator gate rules and the shelf's complaints.

decided.value: No sub-theme reused from a sibling title, and at most a third of a sibling's words reused
decided.reason: KDP removes books whose content is excessively reused across books; his rule keeps two-thirds of any sibling different.

decided.value: No word lists: the brief sets the count per level (for example 25 easy, 25 medium, 25 hard, 25 very hard) and the clue range per level
decided.reason: Sudoku has no theme words; difficulty comes from the clues and the solving steps they force.

decided.value: Claude writes answer words and clues per sub-theme; every clue is checked by a second model solving it cold, and any clue it misses is rewritten
decided.reason: Clue correctness is the highest risk in puzzle books because it needs a reader, not a program.

work: Write each list from the sub-theme; keep a master list of every word used in the book and in every sibling title.
Run the spell check, the trademark check and the inside-another-word check; replace any failing word.
Have a second model (ChatGPT) read each list against its sub-theme and flag words that do not fit.
Alphabetize each list and record it in the book's word file.

output.name: Word file (sub-theme, difficulty, word list per puzzle)
output.format: JSON plus a readable markdown copy

stages.check: Every list passes spelling, fit, length, overlap and trademark checks, and every list is alphabetized.
checks: No word appears inside another word in the same list.
Overlap with every sibling title is a third or less.
stages.if_fail: Replace the failing words and rerun the checks on that list.

stages.title: Generate the grids and run the generator gate
stages.what: Claude's own code builds every grid from its word list, then a separate checker solves each finished grid from scratch and rejects any grid that fails.
stages.why: A missing, doubled or misplaced word makes a puzzle unusable, and filler letters can spell rude words by accident. Free generators often skip these checks.

decided.value: Claude's own Python code, or the free MIT-licensed word-search-generator library, with the checker written separately
decided.reason: Free, repeatable and checkable. Free web generators can require a credit line on every puzzle and written permission to sell.

decided.what: Grid size and directions by level
decided.value: Easy 12 x 12, across and down only; medium 14 x 14, adds diagonals; hard 15 x 15, all eight directions including backwards
decided.reason: His spec is 12 x 12 to 16 x 16. 15 cells at about 0.48 in fit the 7.25 in width left after margins. The direction set must match the how-to page.

decided.value: Every listed word is found exactly once across all eight directions in the final grid
decided.reason: His generator gate.

decided.value: Scan every grid in all eight directions against an offensive-word list (LDNOOBW English list plus brand additions) at 3 letters and up; regenerate the filler on any hit
decided.reason: Accidental rude words in printed word searches do happen; professional tools scan for them.

decided.value: Re-derive the answer key from the final grid, never from the generator's placement log, and compare the two
decided.reason: His generator gate; a wrong key is a repeated complaint.

decided.value: Hash each grid plus its sorted word list and reject any match within the book or any sibling title
decided.reason: KDP's reuse rule and his sibling rule.

decided.value: Generate a full grid, remove clues, and keep a puzzle only when a solver finds exactly one solution; grade difficulty by the solving steps a human-style solver needs, not by clue count alone
decided.reason: A proper sudoku has exactly one solution, and fewer than 17 clues can never give one; clue count alone does not fix difficulty.

decided.value: Grids with 180-degree symmetry, answers of 3 letters or more and no unchecked squares; a second model solves every puzzle from the clues alone before layout
decided.reason: The standard American crossword rules.

decided.value: Each puzzle type runs its own gate; the book groups types into sections and keeps the theme across them
decided.reason: The no-themes complaint applies to mixed books too.

work: Generate each grid with a fixed random seed recorded in the word file, so any grid can be rebuilt.
Run the checker: exactly-once count in eight directions, direction set by level, accidental-word scan, key re-derived and compared, hash against the book and siblings.
Regenerate any failing grid with a new seed until it passes; never hand-edit a grid.
Write the verification report: one line per puzzle with pass or fail on each check.

output.name: Grid file and answer key file
Generator gate report
output.format: CSV plus a one-line summary in the job
output.lands_in: the brand folder, linked on the job in HQ

stages.check: The report shows every puzzle passing every check, with zero accidental-word hits.
checks: The number of puzzles equals the brief's count.
Each level uses only its stated directions.
stages.if_fail: Regenerate the failing grids; if a word list keeps failing, send it back to stage 3.

stages.title: Render the interior and the printable twin
stages.what: Claude lays out the print interior PDF and the printable twin in Letter and A4 from the checked grid file.
stages.why: Large print that is not large, the word list on another page, keys in tiny type and keys placed between puzzles are the shelf's layout complaints; layout settles all of them.

decided.value: 20 to 24 pt bold sans serif capitals (for example Arial or Verdana), never under 18 pt measured at final trim; no italics
decided.reason: APH sets 18 pt as the large-print floor with sans serif and no italics; RNIB calls 18 pt and up giant print.

decided.value: Cells about 0.45 to 0.55 in, lines 0.75 to 1 pt solid black, no gray or color fills
decided.reason: KDP needs lines 0.75 pt or thicker; APH says to avoid gray elements.

decided.value: Same page as its grid, alphabetized, 16 to 18 pt, in two or three columns under the grid, with a check box beside each word
decided.reason: A buyer complained that word lists were not on the puzzle's page; his spec sets 16 to 18 pt.

decided.value: Puzzle number, sub-theme title and difficulty level on every puzzle page; page numbers bold, same size as body text, at the outer corner
decided.reason: His rule that puzzle, title and key numbers agree, and ACB's page-number rule.

decided.value: Behind a divider page at the back, 2 keys per page, letters 14 pt or larger, found words circled with a thin black outline, never color or gray
decided.reason: Keys between puzzles spoil them and colored marks vanish for low-vision readers.

decided.value: Title page, copyright page (with the AI and image credit lines), how-to-play page that names the directions per level, a difficulty key, one filled example
decided.reason: His five-part skeleton puts a how-to page with a filled example up front.

decided.value: Inside 0.75 in, outside 0.5 in, top and bottom 0.5 in, no bleed
decided.reason: Clears KDP's minimum gutter of 0.5 in for 151 to 300 pages and 0.25 in outside.

decided.value: Fonts fully embedded, any images 300 DPI, even page count, no more than 10 blank pages at the end
decided.reason: KDP manuscript rules.

decided.value: The same puzzles and keys as PDF in exact Letter and A4 with all ink inside a 0.5 in margin, plus a start-here page, a terms page and a free 5-puzzle sample; at most 5 files of 20 MB each, names under 70 characters
decided.reason: Etsy file limits and his printable spec; the sample is the brand's lead magnet and Payhip preview.

decided.value: Sudoku: one 9 x 9 grid per page for large print, digits 24 pt or larger, thick 2 pt box lines; crossword: grid and clues on one spread, clue text 16 pt or larger
decided.reason: Same 18 pt floor and same-page rule applied to the other types; practice.

work: Render the interior with ReportLab from the grid file at 8.5 x 11 in.
Render the twin in Letter and A4 from a shared content box of about 7.5 x 10 in, plus the start-here, terms and sample files.
Check fonts with pdffonts and make the page count even (add a notes page or blank page at the end if needed).
Record the final page count; the cover is built from it in stage 7.

output.name: Print interior PDF
output.lands_in: the brand folder, files subfolder, linked on the job in HQ

output.name: Printable twin (Letter, A4, start-here, terms) and 5-puzzle sample

stages.check: The page count is even, all fonts are embedded and every grid and word list sits inside the margins.
checks: Every puzzle page has its word list on the same page.
Answer keys sit only behind the divider.
stages.if_fail: Shrink the cell size within the 0.45 in floor or move the word list into three columns; never drop the letters below 18 pt.

stages.title: Check the finished files page by page
stages.what: Claude reads the grids and keys back out of the finished PDF itself, solves them again, measures the letters and looks at every page as an image.
stages.why: The generator gate checks the data; this checks what the buyer will actually hold. A book can pass the first and still print the wrong key, a doubled page or 16 pt letters. This is the stage the Dog Lover's book restarts at.
inputs: print interior PDF and twin files

decided.value: Extract every grid, word list and key from the PDF text, solve each grid again and compare with the key page
decided.reason: His rule to re-derive the key from the final grid, applied to the final file.

decided.value: Measure the rendered capital height at final trim and confirm 18 pt or larger on puzzle pages and 14 pt or larger on keys
decided.reason: APH's 18 pt floor; his test bench rule to measure at final trim.

decided.value: Every page, including the title, copyright, how-to and divider pages, read by Claude and by a second model
decided.reason: His shared test bench item 6.

decided.value: The puzzle count, page count and point size in the planned title and description match the file
decided.reason: A subtitle promising content the book lacks is a repeated complaint.

decided.value: First recover the three October 16 files from the build chat into the Big Paws Club Drive folder (none were in Drive on November 27). Run this whole stage on them. If they cannot be recovered, or any check fails, regenerate from stage 4 with the saved spec
decided.reason: HQ lists the book as ready to upload, but no check report or proofread exists, and 155 pages is odd, so KDP will count 156 and the spine must be rebuilt.

work: Extract grids, word lists and keys from the PDF with pdfplumber; rerun the exactly-once, direction and accidental-word checks on the extracted grids.
Compare every key page with a fresh solve; confirm puzzle number, title and key number agree page by page.
Measure letter height on rendered pages; render every page to an image and lay them out as a thumbnail grid to catch drift and doubled pages.
Proofread every page; hash the interior against every sibling title.
Fill one puzzle as a tired buyer with reading glasses off: can the first word be found in under a minute from the how-to page alone?
Attach the check report to the job and move HQ's status to needs cover.

output.name: Check report (read-back, key match, letter size, proofread, thumbnail grid, sibling hash)
output.format: PDF report plus a pass line in the job
output.lands_in: the brand folder, linked on the job in HQ

stages.check: Every puzzle read back from the PDF passes, every key matches a fresh solve, and letters measure 18 pt or larger at trim.
checks: The thumbnail grid shows no doubled or blank-by-mistake pages.
The how-to page names exactly the directions the grids use.
stages.if_fail: Fix in the grid file and re-render from stage 5; never patch the PDF by hand.

stages.title: Make and approve the cover
stages.what: An image model makes three front-cover concepts from the brand kit (or Claude builds them around a licensed photo); the owner picks one; Claude builds the full wrap from the final page count.
stages.why: The cover sells at thumbnail size, and older buyers and gift buyers look for the words large print first. A wrap built for a stale page count is the most common late rejection.

choices.question: Which cover do you want?
choices.help: Judge each one at phone thumbnail size, the way shoppers first see it. Large Print must be readable at that size.
choices.generate_from: Three front-cover concepts from the brand kit and the top sellers' cover patterns (never copied), each with LARGE PRINT and the puzzle count in big type, shown at full size and at thumbnail size.

options.label: Concept 1
options.pick_when: Large Print and the puzzle count read clearly at thumbnail size.

options.label: Concept 2
options.pick_when: You want the dog photo or art to lead.

options.label: Concept 3
options.pick_when: You want a sample grid on the front so the format is obvious.

choices.question: Matte or glossy cover?
choices.help: This is the paperback's surface. It is set on the KDP Paperback Content page.

options.label: Matte
options.pick_when: You want less glare for older eyes and a soft gift feel.

options.label: Glossy
options.pick_when: The cover is a bright photo you want to pop.

decided.value: One PDF with back, spine and front built on KDP's template; bleed 0.125 in; images 300 DPI; barcode area at lower right of the back kept clear
decided.reason: KDP cover rules.

decided.value: Even page count x 0.002252 in on white paper; spine text only at 79 pages or more
decided.reason: KDP spine rules. 156 pages gives about 0.351 in.

decided.value: ChatGPT or Muse image generation, both in his plans; a licensed stock photo is fine too. Higgsfield only with his go on credits
decided.reason: AI generation is his default; credit spends need his separate yes.

decided.value: Keep the photo's license line in the rights folder (the Dog Lover's cover uses an Unsplash photo by Janosch Jost)
decided.reason: The Unsplash license allows commercial use without attribution; the record proves where the image came from.

work: Generate or compose the concepts and show them at full and thumbnail size.
Download KDP's cover template for 8.5 x 11, white paper and the exact even page count.
Build the wrap; back cover carries three lines of what is inside, a sample grid image and the brand line; keep the barcode area clear.
Record the prompts, image tool or photo license in the rights folder.
stages.check: The wrap matches the cover calculator's size for the final even page count.
checks: Title, subtitle and author name match the kit exactly.
Large Print and the puzzle count read at thumbnail size.
stages.if_fail: Rebuild the wrap from the current page count; if the page count changed, rebuild every time. If he skips the pick, Claude uses concept 1 and matte.

skip.rule: Concept 1 is used, with a matte finish where a finish applies.

stages.title: Publish it on KDP as a paperback
stages.what: HQ hands over the upload kit: the files, every KDP field in the order the site asks, and the direct link. The owner saves the paperback as a draft, orders a proof if he says yes, checks it, then publishes.
stages.why: Only he may click publish. A printed proof is the one test of whether the letters really read as large print and whether grids sink into the spine.

choices.question: Order a printed proof before publishing?
choices.help: A proof costs the printing cost (about $3.65 for 156 pages at 8.5 x 11) plus shipping, and is stamped Not for Resale. It spends money, so it needs your yes.

options.label: Yes, order one proof (his go required)
options.pick_when: It is the first large-print puzzle book in the family.

options.label: No, publish after the online previewer
options.pick_when: The same layout is already proofed in print, or a holiday date matters more.

choices.question: Paste the Amazon link when the book is live.
choices.help: HQ marks the book live only after you paste the link. Puzzle books can take 3 to 4 weeks in review.

decided.value: Title names the format and audience in plain words; the subtitle carries the checkable promises: puzzle count, letter size, difficulty levels, answer key included (for example: 100 Dog-Themed Puzzles in 24-Point Print, Easy to Hard, Answer Key Included)
decided.reason: His title rule; KDP bans repeated generic words and keyword stuffing; title plus subtitle under 200 characters.

decided.value: Ticked only when the stage 6 check measured 18 pt or more on puzzle pages
decided.reason: The box exists on the Paperback Details page; KDP's threshold for it is not on a public page, so the recipe uses APH's 18 pt, which clears the 16 pt figure reported for the box.

decided.value: On at $12.99 (about $1.54 a copy at 156 pages); off at $9.99, where it pays about $0.34
decided.reason: Expanded Distribution pays 40 percent of list minus printing.

decided.value: Under 4,000 characters including formatting; puzzle count, letter size, levels, theme list, how keys are marked; no web address, no review request, no price
decided.reason: KDP description rules.

decided.value: He clicks Publish. An agent may fill the draft only after a one-tap yes card from him, and the Publish click stays his
decided.reason: His skills never publish or upload; his November 18 request moved the clicks to Claude behind a yes card, so the yes card is kept.

work: Claude: assemble the upload kit (the kit section of this recipe) with every field filled for this book.
Owner: open the new paperback link, paste each field in order, upload the interior and cover, launch the previewer, save as draft.

Owner: request a proof if he said yes, then check it: letters readable at arm's length in ordinary room light, nothing sinking into the spine, keys dark and correct on three random puzzles, page count, cover color.
Owner: press Publish Your Paperback Book.
Claude: move the HQ status to proof ordered, ready to upload, then live only after he pastes the link.

stages.check: The owner has pasted a live Amazon link for the paperback.
checks: The AI-content answer given at upload matches the rights folder.
The low-content box was left unticked.
stages.if_fail: Match KDP's message to the fix list (insufficient gutter, text outside margins, wrong cover size) and return to stage 5 or 7.

skip.rule: Cannot be skipped. Only the owner can press Publish, so the run waits here and shows in Waiting on me.

stages.title: List it as a printable twin on Payhip and Etsy
stages.what: Claude prepares the Payhip product, the free 5-puzzle sample and the Etsy listing; the owner pastes and publishes them.
stages.why: The same puzzles as a PDF reach buyers who print a page at a time for a parent or a care home, and the free sample builds the brand's email list.

decided.value: Payhip first; Etsy once the brand's shop is open; the brand's own store later
decided.reason: His shelf rules, and the Dog Lover's job already names Payhip with Etsy once the shop opens.

ai_question.how_to_answer: Answer from how the book was made. Text: Yes when Claude or another AI wrote the word lists, sub-theme titles, how-to page or clues, which is the default in this recipe. Images: Yes when the cover art or any interior art came from an image model; No when the cover uses a licensed photo and type only (the Dog Lover's cover uses an Unsplash photo). Translations: none. The grids themselves come from an ordinary program placing the words, not an AI-based tool; that reading of KDP's definition is a judgement, so the text answer stays Yes either way.

borrowed.does: Word search, sudoku, crossword and maze generators with print-ready PDF export, plus keyword research and a cover designer
borrowed.how_or_why_not: Claude's code generates and checks every puzzle and lays out the PDF. Book Bolt's pages do not say it guarantees a unique sudoku solution, its exports are image-based, and reviewers report faulty difficulty settings, so its output would still need our checker.
borrowed.price: Pro, which holds the puzzle tools, about $19.99 a month billed yearly or $23.99 month to month (third-party page, November 13, 2026); his go required

borrowed.does: Builds word search grids with set directions, difficulty levels, shapes and an answer key
borrowed.how_or_why_not: Usable as the placing engine; its page does not say it checks each word appears exactly once or scans for rude words, so our checker runs after it.

borrowed.tool: Free web generators (The Teacher's Corner, Discovery Education Puzzlemaker and similar)
borrowed.does: Make one word search at a time in a browser
borrowed.how_or_why_not: Not used: one at a time, no rude-word scan, and The Teacher's Corner requires its credit line on every puzzle and written permission before selling.

borrowed.does: Professional crossword and word search builder with an accidental-word and blacklist check
borrowed.how_or_why_not: Borrowed its check: scan every grid for blacklisted words and for keywords that appear twice. Claude's checker does both.
borrowed.price: Paid desktop software, price not checked; not needed

borrowed.does: Online puzzle book generators that output KDP-ready interiors
borrowed.how_or_why_not: Borrowed their step order (reader, promise, structure, review every puzzle, format, price, upload). Left their large-print sizes: KDPEasy calls 12 to 14 pt large print, below APH's 18 pt floor.
borrowed.price: Credit-based, with a watermark on free use (vendor pages, 2025 and 2026); his go required

borrowed.tool: KDP Print Previewer and cover calculator
borrowed.does: Show how the paperback will print and give the exact wrap size
borrowed.how_or_why_not: Used as is: only Amazon's own tools can say what Amazon will accept.

borrowed.does: Cover and page design with print PDF export
borrowed.how_or_why_not: Image models make the art and Claude builds the wrap on KDP's template; his connected Canva Pro stays optional for hand edits.
